in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I have one child - my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. The location where you're living can affect your eligibility.

**Which country are you currently living in?** 

(Child Benefit may still be available in certain circumstances if you're living in specific countries or if you're a Crown servant working abroad.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Living in Spain may affect your eligibility, but there are some circumstances where you might still qualify.

**Can you tell me about your work situation? Specifically:**
- Are you a Crown servant (such as a civil servant or member of HM Forces)?
- Or are you working for a UK government department or agency abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or working for the UK government. I'm just living here privately.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

One more important question: **Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you an EEA or Swiss national?**

(This can affect whether you might still be eligible for Child Benefit while living in Spain.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have settled or pre-settled status, and I'm not an EEA or Swiss national.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility based on what you've told me.

To clarify before I make my final assessment: **Are you or Alex currently residing in the UK, or are you both living in Spain?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're both living in Spain - Alex lives here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While Alex meets the age requirement (he's 6 years old, which is under 16) and you're clearly responsible for him as you live together, the key issue is the **residency requirement**. 

To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. There are exceptions for people living abroad, such as:
- Crown servants (civil servants, members of HM Forces)
- People working for UK government departments abroad
- Those with certain EU Settlement Scheme statuses
- EEA or Swiss nationals in specific circumstances

Since you're living privately in Spain and don't fall into any of these exception categories, unfortunately you don't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change and you return to live in the UK in the future, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex at that time.
